items.title: Skydance Plans Launch of Bundled Paramount+, HBO Max in Early 2027
items.summary:
Skydance said Monday that it will sell Paramount+ and HBO Max as a single bundled subscription beginning in early 2027, the first major consumer-facing move since the company closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The plan would put series like "Tulsa King" and "The White Lotus" behind one price for the first time.

"Starting in early 2027, consumers will be able to subscribe to both world-class streaming services at an even greater value," the company wrote in a letter to shareholders, adding that it would share more about the bundle and its broader streaming plans in the coming months. Variety reported the details of the letter and the investor call that followed.

The two services bring different libraries to the arrangement. HBO Max carries "Game of Thrones," "The Sopranos," "Euphoria" and the weekly talk shows hosted by Bill Maher and John Oliver, while Paramount+ leans on CBS, Nickelodeon and Comedy Central programming alongside originals including "Landman," "Lioness" and the Star Trek franchise. Combining them is Skydance's attempt to compete more directly with Netflix, Disney+ and Amazon's Prime Video.

Skydance CEO David Ellison framed the bundle as a first step rather than an endpoint, telling investors the two services are complementary and index heavily with different groups of subscribers in the U.S. He suggested a fully combined service could follow over a longer time frame.

The company did not say what happens to existing arrangements that use the same properties. HBO Max has been sold for some time in a bundle with Disney+ and Hulu, and Ellison said on the call that Skydance would review those deals to determine whether they create shareholder value.

items.title: Oasis Won’t Be Attending Rock and Roll of Fame Induction Ceremony
items.summary:
Oasis will not attend Saturday's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony at the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles, and will neither accept the award in person nor perform. Rolling Stone confirmed the band's absence ahead of the event.

Noel Gallagher has booked himself elsewhere that night, playing Goldie's EFG Jazz Festival at London's Royal Festival Hall — his first solo performance since Oasis reunited in 2025, and roughly 5,400 miles from the ceremony. Fans had held out some hope that Liam Gallagher would make the trip on his own. The band is being inducted alongside Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Joy Division/New Order, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan.

The brothers have treated the honor with open skepticism. After the band's first nomination in 2024, Liam told The Sunday Times, "As much as I love Mariah Carey and all that, I want to say: do me a favor and fuck off," comparing the nod to being placed in a rap hall of fame. Oasis made it in the following year, likely boosted by the scale of the reunion tour.

Liam's response on X was its own kind of acceptance speech. "I wanna thank all the people who voted for us it's a real honour ever since I was a little kid and singing in the shower I'd dream about 1 day being in the RnR hall of fame," he wrote, while remaining noncommittal about attending in follow-up posts that invoked his mother's advice to "stop being a dick and go to the awards and behave."

The induction covers a wide roster of members: Liam and Noel, guitarists Paul "Bonehead" Arthurs and Gem Archer, bassists Paul "Guigsy" McGuigan and Andy Bell, and drummers Tony McCarroll and Alan White. Arthurs, Archer and Bell play in the current touring lineup, while McGuigan, McCarroll and White have not performed with the band in years.

It remains unclear whether any former members will appear or how the Hall will mark the band's induction without them. Oasis join a long roll of absentees that includes Paul McCartney, David Bowie, Joni Mitchell, the Sex Pistols, Roger Waters and the Sex Pistols' fellow refusers Van Morrison and Axl Rose.

items.title: Paul McCartney Becomes a Billionaire, Making Him the World’s Third-Richest Musician
items.summary:
Forbes has valued Paul McCartney's net worth at approximately $1.4 billion, placing him among the world's billionaires for the first time. The designation came with the launch of the magazine's new newsletter, The Billie, and makes McCartney the third-richest musician on the planet behind Jay-Z at $2.8 billion and Taylor Swift at $2 billion.

The bulk of the fortune traces to MLP Communications, the publishing company McCartney started in 1969, which administers his own catalog along with copyrights belonging to other artists. Forbes found that his acquisitions — catalogs from artists including Buddy Holly, plus Broadway scores and Christmas standards — account for nearly a quarter of a billion dollars on their own.

The Beatles remain a substantial piece of it. As one of four partners in Apple Corps, McCartney takes 25 percent of a holding company that generates roughly $50 million a year from streaming, vinyl and merchandise, an income stream Forbes estimates is worth more than $150 million to each member or estate. His share of Beatles songwriting copyrights, which he spent two decades in legal fights to secure, brings in about $10 million annually and is worth at least $200 million, Variety noted in its write-up of the Forbes figures.

Touring, property and art fill out the rest. McCartney's Got Back tour ran 79 shows between 2022 and 2025, and his holdings include real estate around the world and an art collection with works by Magritte and Picasso.

He has not slowed down. McCartney released his 20th solo album, "The Boys of Dungeon Lane," in May, and he is the subject of "Man on the Run," Morgan Neville's documentary about his life after the Beatles broke up and his years fronting Wings.
